data.overview: F-2 makes every static stub in the F-1 shell (RectifyWindowShell/ShellToolbar/ShellStatusBar/StageSurface) live for Android: launch-time adb/idb tool detection, the Android/iOS platform switch (Android functional, iOS detection-only), a device picker covering Physical and Emulator sources with inline emulator Boot, a 'Start mirroring' action, the 2s-polling passive NO-SIGNAL empty state, and a status bar reporting tool version/resolution/fps/latency. The hardest and most consequential open question is how the live Android screen actually reaches StageSurface's content slot inside the <150ms NFR-1 target — this clarify stage mints a staged, honest answer (screenshot polling now, documented as not meeting NFR-1, with the H.264-decode path explicitly deferred) rather than promising a number nothing on the classpath today can deliver.
data.problemStatement: Rectify's canonical window exists (F-1) but shows nothing real: the platform switch, device indicator, and status bar are static previews, and StageSurface has no content source. Until a real Android device can be discovered and mirrored inside the single canonical window, there is no product to annotate — every downstream spec (annotation, measurement, payload, error recovery) depends on this one being live.
data.purpose: Deliver a working, demoable Android discovery-to-mirror pipeline (detect tools -> pick a device -> start mirroring -> see live stats) built entirely on F-1's slot contracts, reusing rectify-poc's proven adb parsing/screenshot logic behind this repo's Failure/resultLauncher error-handling and data->domain->presentation layering, while being explicit about which latency target it can and cannot hit in v1.
goals: GOAL-1: Android becomes a real, selectable live mirror source inside the single canonical Rectify window within this spec's scope (FR-1..FR-5) — the product's entry point stops being a stub.

GOAL-5: Interaction over the mirror stays responsive enough for the annotation workflow (drag-to-freeze) that depends on it; this spec is explicit that v1's chosen transport (staged, see FR-24) does not yet meet the <150ms NFR-1 target and documents the follow-up path rather than silently falling short.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given adb and idb are installed, when the app launches, then the toolbar shows a status dot reflecting detected tool versions for both platforms.
Given a physical device is connected and an emulator is running, when the device picker is opened, then both appear in distinct Physical/Emulator sections and arrow keys plus Enter select an entry.
Given a device is selected in the picker, when the user clicks 'Start mirroring', then the live mirror begins streaming.
Given no device is connected, when adb polling runs, then the 'NO SIGNAL' state shows with guidance text and an inline emulator picker plus Boot button.
Given live mirror is active, then the status bar displays current tool version, resolution, fps, and latency, updating at least once per second.

Given adb is not found on PATH at launch, when tool detection runs, then F-2 exposes a typed ToolMissing discovery state (and reflects it as an offline/warning toolbar status dot) for error-handling-and-recovery (F-3) to render as the actionable error card (comp 04) — F-2 itself does not build the Locate-adb/Retry/Copy UI.

Given adb is installed but reports zero attached devices across repeated polls, when polling runs, then F-2 exposes a typed NoDeviceFound discovery state carrying poll metadata (last-poll time, attempt count) for F-3 to render the escalated error card (comp 05, Restart adb / Boot emulator instead) — F-2's own stage still shows only the passive NO SIGNAL state from AC-4.

Given no device has ever been selected, when the app has focus, then the device picker renders as a centered panel filling the stage's content slot on Theme.color.bg (not the dotted stage background), matching comps 01/03; given a device is already selected, clicking the toolbar DeviceChip reopens the same panel. There is no separate small anchored dropdown menu implementation.

Given any adb/idb command needs to run, then it is issued only through the single device-scoped command executor, whose API requires an already-resolved device id as a non-optional parameter — no code path in the codebase can construct or issue a device command without one (NFR-5 enforced by API shape).

Given live mirror is active, then the status bar shows tool version and resolution unconditionally, fps reflecting the active transport's real achieved rate, and latency either as a real measurement or an explicit placeholder (never a fabricated number) when the active transport cannot measure it end-to-end — all updating at least once per second.

functionalRequirements.text: On launch, detect installed adb and idb tool versions and show a status dot per platform in the toolbar.
Show a platform switch (Android/iOS) in the toolbar on every screen; Android is functional in v1, iOS is deferred to v1.1+.
Provide a device picker dropdown with Physical-device and Emulator sections (running, or shut-down with an inline Boot button), navigable via arrow keys and Enter.
Provide a primary 'Start mirroring' action that connects to the selected device and begins the live mirror stream.
When no device is connected, poll adb every 2s and show a 'NO SIGNAL' empty state with guidance to plug in a USB-debug device or boot an emulator inline.
Show a status bar with live stream stats: tool version, resolution, fps, and latency.

v1 ships a screenshot-polling mirror transport (adb exec-out screencap, reusing rectify-poc's proven capture/foldable-trim logic) as the FR-4 stream source; it is explicitly documented as not meeting NFR-1's <150ms target. An H.264-decode transport (scrcpy-server socket consumed in-JVM) is a deliberate v1.1+ follow-up, gated on choosing and justifying a new JVM decoder dependency per version-catalog-hygiene.md.

The live mirror transport is abstracted behind a single interface consumed by StageSurface's content slot and by FR-22's stats contract, so swapping the v1 polling transport for a future decoder-based transport (FR-24) requires no change to the shell integration or the stats shape.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Live mirror glass-to-glass latency should stay low enough (target under ~150ms) that drag-to-select and freeze feel responsive.
adb/idb commands are only ever invoked against the user's explicitly selected, connected device — never an arbitrary or remote target.
Device picker, annotation popovers, and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers).
v1 targets macOS only; no Windows/Linux builds.

outOfScope: Functional iOS mirroring (FR-2 defers it to v1.1+; the switch exists and shows detected idb only).

The rich error-card UI and recovery actions for comps 04/05 (Locate adb, Copy, Retry, Restart adb, Boot-emulator-instead) — owned by error-handling-and-recovery (F-3), which consumes F-2's typed discovery states (AC-41, AC-42).
Annotation, measurement, payload, history, and MCP specs (later in the roadmap).
Recovery/reconnect UX for a mirror that disconnects mid-session after FR-4 has already started streaming — pre-connection discovery only is this spec's scope; mid-session recovery is F-3 territory.
A production H.264-decode transport that actually meets the <150ms NFR-1 target in v1 — staged out per FR-24; tracked as an explicit follow-up, not silently dropped.

constraints.text: No JVM H.264 decoder exists on the classpath today (verified against gradle/libs.versions.toml) — adding one is a new-dependency decision requiring explicit justification against version-catalog-hygiene.md, and is deferred past v1 (see FR-24).

All adb/idb process execution must route through a single device-scoped command executor whose API requires a resolved device id (NFR-5) — no repository or use case may shell out directly (see AC-44).
Kotlin daemon is capped at 3GB; building this spec's three affected KMP modules across all targets simultaneously OOMs the 18GB build host — build per module during implementation.
PRD estimates this spec as 'L'; the staged transport plan (FR-24) keeps the build inside that envelope by deferring the highest-cost item (in-JVM H.264 decode) rather than absorbing it into v1.

assumptions.text: scrcpy 3.3.1 and adb remain available via PATH/Homebrew-standard locations during implementation and demo; detection logic reads PATH dynamically rather than hardcoding the exact verified paths from this machine.

No physical Android device or running emulator is guaranteed available in the automated build/test environment; AC-2/AC-3/AC-44's 'test' verification is achieved by mocking the process-execution/device-list boundary, not by requiring real hardware in CI.

Shipping screenshot-polling as the v1 mirror transport (not meeting NFR-1) is an acceptable, explicitly-flagged v1 trade-off rather than a silent shortfall — this clarify stage surfaces it for the plan stage and any human review rather than deciding alone that the gap is acceptable forever.

presentation-core-ui's existing SourceListRow molecule is a reasonable starting point for the device-picker's Physical/Emulator rows (radio + trailing slot variants); exact fit is confirmed at plan/design stage per design-tokens.md's 'browse before authoring' rule rather than assumed finished here.

dependencies.note: Merged to development; provides RectifyWindowShell/ShellToolbar/ShellStatusBar/StageSurface slot contracts this spec fills.
Downstream dependent; inherits the ToolMissing/NoDeviceFound discovery-state contract (AC-41, AC-42) to render comps 04 and 05.
Reference implementation only (not a build dependency) for adb devices -l parsing, screencap capture, and wm/getprop device-info logic.

scenarios.title: First-run setup and tool detection
steps: Detect adb/idb and show status dots
Open device picker showing Physical/Emulator sections
Select a device via keyboard or click

scenarios.title: No device connected (empty state)
steps: Show NO SIGNAL placeholder with guidance
Offer inline emulator picker + Boot button

scenarios.title: adb not on PATH at launch
steps: Launch app with adb not on PATH
F-3 renders the actionable error card (comp 04) from that state

scenarios.title: adb present, zero devices sustained across polls
steps: Repeated 2s polls each report zero attached devices
F-2's stage continues showing the passive NO SIGNAL state (AC-4)
F-2 emits NoDeviceFound with poll metadata
F-3 renders the escalated error card (comp 05) from that state

successMetrics: All six in-scope FRs (FR-1..FR-5, FR-22) are demoable end to end: launch -> tool dots -> picker -> Start mirroring -> live polling stream in StageSurface -> status bar stats updating >=1/s.
Device discovery/parsing logic (listDevices, deviceInfo) is covered by unit tests against fake adb output, with no physical device required in CI (AC-2 'test' path).
No new runtime dependency is added without an explicit version-catalog-hygiene.md justification recorded at plan stage (FR-24's decoder deferral).
openQuestions: Measured or cited glass-to-glass latency for scrcpy-server + in-JVM H.264 decode is still unknown — the plan/a spike should get a real number before committing to it as the v1.1+ follow-up implied by FR-24/FR-25.

Whether v1's UI should visibly indicate to the user that the stream is polling-based and not meeting the 150ms target (vs. staying silent) is a UX-writing decision outside this clarify stage's scope — flagged for plan stage.

Whether SourceListRow needs new props/states for the picker's radio + trailing-slot variants (Running dot / Boot button / Android-version+USB) or a new molecule is warranted — plan stage confirms via full kit/ browsing per design-tokens.md.

proposedSurvey.question: Q1 — The live-mirror transport (FR-4, NFR-1 <150ms): which does v1 ship?
options: A. Screenshot polling (adb exec-out screencap, reusing rectify-poc logic) behind a MirrorTransport interface now; scrcpy-server + in-JVM H.264 decode is an explicit, separately-scoped v1.1+ follow-up (staged).
B. Build scrcpy-server + in-JVM H.264 decode now, in this spec, despite no H.264 decoder existing on the classpath today.
C. Launch scrcpy as a child process in its own OS window.
D. adb exec-out screenrecord --output-format=h264 + decode now.
proposedSurvey.recommended: A. Screenshot polling (adb exec-out screencap, reusing rectify-poc logic) behind a MirrorTransport interface now; scrcpy-server + in-JVM H.264 decode is an explicit, separately-scoped v1.1+ follow-up (staged).
proposedSurvey.rationale: Checked gradle/libs.versions.toml: there is no media/codec/H.264 dependency anywhere in this repo today. Option B is the only one that could plausibly hit <150ms inside StageSurface, but it requires picking and justifying a brand-new dependency (version-catalog-hygiene.md), implementing a socket protocol against scrcpy's server, and building a decode pipeline — a multi-week effort disproportionate to this spec's PRD 'L' estimate and to F-2's actual scope (discovery + first connection, not a media pipeline). Option C composites in a separate OS window, which does not render inside Rectify's stage at all and breaks the canonical single-window architecture F-1 just established (FR-11/AC-12) — disqualifying regardless of latency. Option D still needs the same missing decoder as B, with worse device-side encoder quirks and no scrcpy tooling benefit. Option A reuses proven, already-read poc logic, ships something real and demoable for every FR in scope, and is explicit on a 'not yet meeting NFR-1' gap rather than quietly failing it or over-building to chase a number this spec cannot safely deliver. FR-24/FR-25 encode this as a staged, interface-isolated decision so the follow-up is a transport swap, not a rewrite.

proposedSurvey.question: Q2 — The F-3 boundary: which error surfaces does F-2 itself render, and what does F-3 inherit?
options: A. F-2 renders only the passive NO SIGNAL state (comp 02, literal AC-4 text) and the toolbar status dot; F-2 exposes typed ToolMissing/NoDeviceFound discovery states that F-3 consumes to render BOTH rich error cards (comp 04 adb-not-on-PATH, comp 05 no-device-detected) and their recovery actions (Locate adb, Copy, Retry, Restart adb, Boot emulator instead).
B. F-2 renders comp 02 and comp 05 (treating 'no device found' as one feature with an escalated variant); F-3 owns only comp 04 (tool-missing, a pre-device-loop gate).
C. F-2 renders all of comp 02/04/05 fully; F-3 handles only post-connection/mid-session errors, not discovery errors at all.
proposedSurvey.recommended: A. F-2 renders only the passive NO SIGNAL state (comp 02, literal AC-4 text) and the toolbar status dot; F-2 exposes typed ToolMissing/NoDeviceFound discovery states that F-3 consumes to render BOTH rich error cards (comp 04 adb-not-on-PATH, comp 05 no-device-detected) and their recovery actions (Locate adb, Copy, Retry, Restart adb, Boot emulator instead).
proposedSurvey.rationale: AC-4's literal PRD text ('NO SIGNAL state shows with guidance text and an inline emulator picker plus Boot button') matches comp 02 exactly and says nothing about Locate-adb/Copy/Retry/Restart-adb actions — those only appear in comps 04 and 05. Both 04 and 05 are built from the same generic 'diagnose and recover an environment problem' chrome (a command to copy, a locate/restart/retry action, a footer diagnostic line) that is cross-cutting by nature — it will also apply to idb failures later, which is precisely what error-handling-and-recovery exists to own. Splitting at option B still forces F-2 to build one of the two generic error-card UIs, duplicating chrome F-3 will build anyway for comp 04; option C makes F-3 depend on F-2 for nothing, contradicting the PRD's stated dependency direction. Option A keeps F-2's surface to literal AC-4, gives F-3 a clean typed-state contract to consume, and avoids building error-card UI in two places.

proposedSurvey.question: Q3 — Device-picker surface: full-stage takeover, toolbar dropdown, or both? (reconciling FR-3's word 'dropdown' against comps 01/03)
options: A. Single full-stage takeover panel rendered in StageSurface's content slot, centered on Theme.color.bg (not the dotted stage) as comps 01/03 show — shown automatically pre-first-selection and reopened by clicking the toolbar DeviceChip.
B. A true small anchored dropdown/popover from the toolbar DeviceChip, literally matching FR-3's word 'dropdown', built separately from the first-run full-panel state.
C. Both: a separate first-run full panel AND a separate in-toolbar dropdown menu, each with their own Physical/Emulator list rendering.
proposedSurvey.recommended: A. Single full-stage takeover panel rendered in StageSurface's content slot, centered on Theme.color.bg (not the dotted stage) as comps 01/03 show — shown automatically pre-first-selection and reopened by clicking the toolbar DeviceChip.
proposedSurvey.rationale: Comps 01 and 03 show a centered panel with full section headers, tool-version cards with paths/Xcode versions, grouped device rows, and keyboard hints — filling the entire content region, not a small popover a dropdown menu could ever hold. FR-3's word 'dropdown' is PRD shorthand for 'a selectable list the user opens,' not a literal small anchored menu; overriding the word against two consistent visual comps is the defensible read. A single component reused for both the automatic first-run entry and the DeviceChip-triggered reopen (option A) avoids duplicating Physical/Emulator list rendering (option C's cost) and fits StageSurface's existing single `content` slot without adding new shell-level surfaces.

proposedSurvey.question: Q4 — Process execution layering: where does the 'adb/idb only ever targets the selected device' constraint (NFR-5) live, and how is it enforced?
options: A. A dedicated device-scoped command executor in the data layer, whose every method signature requires an already-resolved deviceId (no overload omits it); it is the only thing in the codebase allowed to shell out; repository implementations call it, domain/presentation never do.
B. No dedicated executor — each data-*-impl repository builds its own ProcessBuilder calls inline, passing the selected device id through at each call site.
C. Put the executor in domain-usecase-impl, next to the use cases that need it.
proposedSurvey.recommended: A. A dedicated device-scoped command executor in the data layer, whose every method signature requires an already-resolved deviceId (no overload omits it); it is the only thing in the codebase allowed to shell out; repository implementations call it, domain/presentation never do.
proposedSurvey.rationale: NFR-5 explicitly asks that commands 'never target an arbitrary or remote target' — the only way to make that true by construction rather than by convention is an API shape where it is impossible to call without a device id (option A), not trusting every call site to remember (option B is exactly the call-site-discipline NFR-5 warns against). Per domain-layer.md, shelling out to adb/idb is infrastructure I/O, which belongs in the data layer behind a repository, not in domain-usecase-impl (option C misplaces I/O one layer too high and makes `domain-usecase-impl` depend on process details it shouldn't know about). A single executor is also the natural place to add FR-24's transport abstraction later without touching call sites.

proposedSurvey.question: Q5 — FR-22/AC-25 status bar stats: what does v1 actually show for each of tool version / resolution / fps / latency, given Q1's transport choice?
options: A. Tool version and resolution shown unconditionally (available regardless of transport); fps reflects the real achieved rate of the active transport (poll rate in v1); latency shows an explicit placeholder ('—'/'n/a') rather than a fabricated number when the active transport cannot measure true glass-to-glass latency.
B. Show all four fields unconditionally, approximating latency in polling mode as 'time since last successful poll' even though that is not true glass-to-glass latency.
C. Drop the latency field from v1 entirely; ship only tool version/resolution/fps.
proposedSurvey.recommended: A. Tool version and resolution shown unconditionally (available regardless of transport); fps reflects the real achieved rate of the active transport (poll rate in v1); latency shows an explicit placeholder ('—'/'n/a') rather than a fabricated number when the active transport cannot measure true glass-to-glass latency.
proposedSurvey.rationale: AC-25 requires all four fields to be present and updating at least once per second, but does not require latency to be a real measurement in v1 — option B would actively misinform users about whether NFR-1 is met by labeling a different quantity ('time since last poll') as latency, which is worse than an honest placeholder given this spec's own staged, NFR-1-non-compliant transport decision (Q1). Option C silently drops a field AC-25 explicitly names, for no benefit over a placeholder. Option A keeps the stat bar's four-field contract stable (FR-25's transport-swap abstraction) so a future decoder transport (FR-24 follow-up) only has to fill in a real number, not add a new field.

survey.rationale: AC-25 requires all four fields to be present and updating at least once per second, but does not require latency to be a real measurement in v1 — option B would actively misinform users about whether NFR-1 is met by labeling a different quantity ('time since last poll') as latency, which is worse than an honest placeholder given this spec's own staged, NFR-1-non-compliant transport decision (Q1). Option C silently drops a field AC-25 explicitly names, for no benefit over a placeholder. Option A keeps the stat bar's four-field contract stable (FR-25's transport-swap abstraction) so a future decoder transport (FR-24 follow-up) only has to fill in a real number, not add a new field. || Autonomous run. Q1 is the consequential one: v1 ships screenshot polling behind a MirrorTransport interface, which means v1 KNOWINGLY DOES NOT MEET NFR-1's <150ms target. Accepted because no H.264 decoder exists anywhere in the repo (verified against gradle/libs.versions.toml), building one is disproportionate to this deliverable, and the staged interface keeps the real transport a drop-in replacement. This is recorded as a deliberate NFR-1 waiver, not an oversight, and is surfaced to the operator in the final chain report.
